section_summary: This section covers internal political and economic developments in Japan between July and October 1939, centered on wartime mobilization, national psychology, and a major government transition. It records the promulgation of the National Draft Ordinance for compulsory labor mobilization under the National General Mobilization Law and the establishment of the Asia Promotion Commission to advise on China policy. Following the conclusion of the German-Soviet Non-Aggression Pact, the Cabinet of Baron Kiichiro Hiranuma resigned en bloc out of responsibility to the Throne, leading the Court group around the Emperor to install an 'inner cabinet' under General Nobuyuki Abe charged with pursuing an independent foreign policy free of European entanglements. Accompanying Embassy despatches and State Department analyses examine Japanese public morale, the rise of state socialism, and Japan's critical economic dependence on American raw materials upon the outbreak of war in Europe.

subfiles.about: Division memorandum analyzing Japanese press propaganda, public attitudes toward Germany and Great Britain, and respect for American protests.
subfiles.from: Division of Far Eastern Affairs (Joseph W. Ballantine)
subfiles.summary: Continuing Despatch 4000's morale analysis: propaganda entrenched hostility toward Britain, enthusiasm for Germany stopped short of partnership, no formal German alliance after Roosevelt's April message to Hitler, and American disapproval bred mixed respect and resentment.
subfiles.title: Division of Far Eastern Affairs Memorandum on Japanese State of Mind and Foreign Policy

subfiles.about: Comprehensive Embassy report analyzing Japanese public morale, wartime economic conditions, susceptibility to propaganda, and relations with foreign powers after two years of war in China.
subfiles.from: Eugene H. Dooman (Chargé d'Affaires ad interim, American Embassy, Tokyo)
subfiles.summary: Drafted by Second Secretary Cabot Coville, Tokyo despatch no. 4000 reviews the Japanese state of mind on the second anniversary of the China Incident. The report observes that initial flag-waving has evolved into sober, fatalistic determination comparable to facing natural disasters, supported by an industrial war boom that keeps labor contented while squeezing business and salaried classes. Despite successful official indoctrination using abstract slogans, the population suffers from a growing consciousness of international censure and isolation. Furthermore, while bitter resentment against Great Britain is entrenched, fundamental public goodwill toward the United States persists, and persistent American protests continue to command Japanese respect.
subfiles.title: Tokyo Despatch No. 4000: 'The Present State of Mind of Japan'

subfiles.about: Instruction transmitting State Department commendation to Second Secretary Cabot Coville for his lucid report on the Japanese public state of mind.
subfiles.from: Sumner Welles (For the Secretary of State, Washington)
subfiles.summary: Welles commends Despatch 4000's drafter Coville for careful, lucid analysis of a complex subject, directing a copy to him given his absence from Tokyo.
subfiles.title: Instruction No. 1800 to Tokyo Commending Despatch No. 4000
subfiles.to: Eugene H. Dooman (American Chargé d'Affaires ad interim, Tokyo)

subfiles.about: Departmental memorandum summarizing Embassy Tokyo's report on the establishment of the Asia Promotion Commission.
subfiles.from: Division of Far Eastern Affairs (Warner)
subfiles.summary: Memo reviews Despatch 4035 on the July 1939 Asia Promotion Commission, calling it 'a board to watch a board' born of Cabinet-bureaucracy conflict, showing Japanese disunity over China policy.
subfiles.title: Division of Far Eastern Affairs Memorandum on Creation of Asia Promotion Commission
subfiles.to: Joseph W. Ballantine and Laurence E. Salisbury (Far Eastern Affairs)

subfiles.about: Despatch reporting the promulgation of Imperial Ordinance No. 438 creating the Asia Promotion Commission to advise on China policy, transmitting translation of the ordinance.
subfiles.from: Eugene H. Dooman (Chargé d'Affaires ad interim, American Embassy, Tokyo)
subfiles.summary: Drafted by Third Secretary Frank A. Schuler, Jr., this despatch analyzes the creation of the Asia Promotion Commission under Imperial Ordinance No. 438 as a supreme advisory organ to the Asia Promotion Board. The 50-member body includes prominent industrial, academic, and administrative figures such as Yosuke Matsuoka, Shozo Murata, Dr. Hantaro Nagaoka, and Shingo Tsuda, but largely duplicates existing ministerial liaison committees. The Embassy notes that the commission reflects bureaucratic confusion and serves primarily to diffuse governmental responsibility. A complete translation of Imperial Ordinance No. 438 is enclosed.
subfiles.title: Tokyo Despatch No. 4035: 'Creation of Asia Promotion Commission'

subfiles.about: Cross-reference file sheet noting a report from the Consulate at Tsingtao on the establishment of a local Asia Affairs Board office.
subfiles.from: Samuel Sokobin (American Consulate, Tsingtao)
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: Tsingtao despatch on the March 1939 Asia Affairs Board branch office opening, with consular comments.
subfiles.title: Document File Note: Japanese Asia Affairs Board Office in Tsingtao

subfiles.about: Departmental staff memorandum assessing Embassy Tokyo's report on compulsory labor conscription and the shift toward state socialism in Japan.
subfiles.from: Division of Far Eastern Affairs (Warner)
subfiles.summary: Memo reviews Despatch 4056 on the National Draft Ordinance under the Mobilization Act, framing labor conscription as an expanding, bloodless-revolution-style shift toward state socialism amid China-war demands.
subfiles.title: Division of Far Eastern Affairs Memorandum on Labor Conscription Measure

subfiles.about: Comprehensive report and legal translations regarding the National Draft Ordinance and Welfare Ministry regulations enforcing compulsory labor conscription.
subfiles.from: Eugene H. Dooman (Chargé d'Affaires ad interim, American Embassy, Tokyo)
subfiles.summary: Despatch no. 4056, prepared by Frank A. Schuler, Jr., reports the promulgation of Imperial Ordinance No. 451 enforcing Article 4 of the National General Mobilization Law. The ordinance empowers the Welfare Minister to draft skilled technicians and laborers registered under vocational registration ordinances into war industries to overcome severe personnel shortages. The despatch explains that this legislation, modeled heavily on German labor controls, represents a permanent step toward state socialism and amounts to a bloodless revolution. Enclosed are English translations of Imperial Ordinance No. 451 (enacted July 7, 1939, covering Japan Proper, Chosen, Taiwan, Karafuto, and the South Sea Islands) and Welfare Ministry Ordinance No. 17 (promulgated July 11, 1939) detailing draft procedures, exemptions, compensation, and summonses.
subfiles.title: Tokyo Despatch No. 4056: 'Promulgation of Labor Conscription Measure'

subfiles.about: Telegraphic report on the fall of the Hiranuma Cabinet and the selection of General Nobuyuki Abe to head an independent foreign policy.
subfiles.from: Eugene H. Dooman (Chargé d'Affaires ad interim, American Embassy, Tokyo)
subfiles.summary: Dooman reports General Abe forming a Cabinet after Hiranuma's fall, with moderates exploiting military miscalculation over Europe to regain foreign-policy control; Abe was chosen for personal suitability to pursue an 'independent' policy, outcome in China uncertain.
subfiles.title: Tokyo Telegram No. 445 on Cabinet Crisis and Selection of General Abe

subfiles.about: Confidential Department paraphrase of Tokyo telegram no. 445 on the resignation of the Hiranuma Cabinet and General Abe's selection.
subfiles.from: Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.summary: Paraphrase of telegram 445: Hiranuma's fall stemmed from European miscalculations, letting Throne-aligned moderates reclaim policy; the Cabinet resigned jointly, and Abe was picked to pursue an independent, Europe-disentangled foreign policy.
subfiles.title: Confidential Paraphrase of Tokyo Telegram No. 445

subfiles.about: Telegraphic report on press praise for Hiranuma's principled resignation and the political maneuvers behind General Abe's selection.
subfiles.from: Eugene H. Dooman (Chargé d'Affaires ad interim, American Embassy, Tokyo)
subfiles.summary: Dooman reports press praised Hiranuma's resignation over missing the German-Soviet pact; after a collective resignation, Court advisers Konoe, Makino, and Yuasa chose Abe as unifying, with speculation on better Western ties and a dismissed Soviet nonaggression idea.
subfiles.title: Tokyo Telegram No. 446 on Press Reaction and Political Maneuvers Behind Abe Cabinet

subfiles.about: Telegraphic announcement of the ministerial roster and concurrent portfolio appointments in the new Abe Cabinet.
subfiles.from: Eugene H. Dooman (Chargé d'Affaires ad interim, American Embassy, Tokyo)
subfiles.summary: Telegram announces Abe's Cabinet, holding Foreign Affairs pending Shigemitsu's arrival, with Hata (War), Yoshida (Navy), Obara (Home/Welfare), Aoki (Finance/Planning), Godo (Commerce/Agriculture), Nagai (Communications/Railways), Kawarada (Education), Kanemitsu (Overseas), and Endo (Cabinet Secretary).
subfiles.title: Tokyo Telegram No. 447 Announcing Composition of the Abe Cabinet

subfiles.about: Report on the formal investiture of the Abe Cabinet and press appraisal of its members as an inner cabinet of nonentities.
subfiles.from: Eugene H. Dooman (Chargé d'Affaires ad interim, American Embassy, Tokyo)
subfiles.summary: Dooman reports Abe's Cabinet formally appointed; press welcomed the quick 'inner cabinet' but called it nonentities, viewed Abe as untested but honest, worried over Aoki's Finance appointment, and awaited his foreign-policy statement.
subfiles.title: Tokyo Telegram No. 448 on Investiture and Press Reaction to Abe Cabinet

subfiles.about: Report summarizing Prime Minister Abe's first radio broadcast and policy statement to the nation, with press commentary.
subfiles.from: Eugene H. Dooman (Chargé d'Affaires ad interim, American Embassy, Tokyo)
subfiles.summary: Telegram summarizes Abe's radio address reaffirming a 'new order in East Asia,' pledging independent cooperation with supportive nations and firmness against opponents; press called it vague and doubted his execution plan.
subfiles.title: Tokyo Telegram No. 449 on Prime Minister Abe's Radio Address

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet indexing a Tokyo telegram reporting that Prince Konoe and Count Makino are directing plans for the Cabinet transition.
subfiles.from: Eugene H. Dooman (American Embassy, Tokyo)
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: Tokyo telegram notes plans for Japan's government transition rest with Prince Konoe and Count Makino.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference File Note on Impending Japanese Government Transition

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet indexing a telegram from Paris reporting intelligence that the Japanese Government might fall.
subfiles.from: William C. Bullitt (American Embassy, Paris)
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: Paris telegram from Bullitt notes diplomatic information that Japan's government might fall due to European developments.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference File Note on European Reports of Japanese Government Instability

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet indexing a telegram reporting the morning resignation of the entire Japanese Cabinet.
subfiles.from: Eugene H. Dooman (American Embassy, Tokyo)
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: Tokyo telegram reports the entire Japanese Cabinet resigned on the morning of August 28, 1939.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference File Note on Resignation of Japanese Cabinet

subfiles.about: Urgent telegram reporting the resignation of the Hiranuma Cabinet and the Imperial command to General Abe to form a new ministry.
subfiles.from: Eugene H. Dooman (Chargé d'Affaires ad interim, American Embassy, Tokyo)
subfiles.summary: Dooman reports Japan's entire Cabinet resigned August 28, 1939, with the Emperor calling on General Abe to form a new one.
subfiles.title: Tokyo Telegram No. 442 Reporting Cabinet Resignation and Imperial Command to General Abe

subfiles.about: Telegram analyzing Japan's diplomatic prudence toward the European war and transmitting Commercial Attaché Williams's findings on critical dependence on American supplies.
subfiles.from: Eugene H. Dooman (Chargé d'Affaires ad interim, American Embassy, Tokyo)
subfiles.summary: Dooman reports Japan's Foreign Office undecided on the European crisis as Abe prioritizes settling China; long-term anti-Russia tradition favors U.S./British friendship, and Williams's study shows Europe's war will make America essential for oil, steel, and cotton, or Japan's industry collapses.
subfiles.title: Tokyo Telegram No. 450 on Foreign Policy and Commercial Effects of European War

subfiles.about: Departmental paraphrase of Tokyo telegram no. 450 analyzing Japan's economic reliance on the United States upon the outbreak of European war.
subfiles.from: Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.summary: Paraphrase of telegram 450: Williams's study finds European trade disruption will make the U.S. Japan's chief source of iron, oil, machinery, and cotton, pushing Japan toward restored relations with democratic powers for economic reasons.
subfiles.title: Confidential Paraphrase of Tokyo Telegram No. 450

subfiles.about: Staff memorandum proposing an official instruction of commendation for Third Secretary Frank A. Schuler, Jr., for drafting Tokyo Despatch No. 4126.
subfiles.from: Laurence E. Salisbury (Division of Far Eastern Affairs)
subfiles.summary: Salisbury recommends commending Third Secretary Schuler for drafting over half the Embassy's recent despatches, praising his Cabinet-change report's preparation, clarity, and language.
subfiles.title: Division of Far Eastern Affairs Memorandum Recommending Commendation of Frank A. Schuler, Jr.

subfiles.about: Staff circulation memorandum summarizing Tokyo Despatch No. 4126 regarding the causes of Hiranuma's resignation and the installation of the Abe Cabinet.
subfiles.from: Laurence E. Salisbury (Division of Far Eastern Affairs)
subfiles.summary: Memo circulates Despatch 4126: Hiranuma resigned to take Throne responsibility for missing the German-Soviet pact and redefine premier-Emperor relations; Abe's choice, engineered by Konoe, Makino, and Yuasa, shows the Court group retains real power.
subfiles.title: Division of Far Eastern Affairs Memorandum Summarizing Tokyo Despatch No. 4126
subfiles.to: Far Eastern Affairs Officers (JP, MOM, A, WA, PA/H, JWB)

subfiles.about: Comprehensive analytical despatch on the constitutional, factional, and international factors surrounding Hiranuma's resignation and the formation of the Abe Cabinet.
subfiles.from: Eugene H. Dooman (Chargé d'Affaires ad interim, American Embassy, Tokyo)
subfiles.summary: Despatch no. 4126, drafted by Frank A. Schuler, Jr., provides an exhaustive analysis of the Cabinet crisis precipitated by the German-Soviet Non-Aggression Pact. For months Premier Hiranuma and Navy Minister Mitsumasa Yonai had successfully resisted War Minister Seishiro Itagaki's push for an Axis alliance, but the pact rendered Hiranuma's reports to the Emperor erroneous, prompting his resignation to uphold the dignity of the Throne. Genro Prince Saionji was bypassed as the Court group—Lord Keeper of the Privy Seal Kurahei Yuasa, Prince Konoe, and Count Makino—eliminated Koki Hirota and Kazushige Ugaki and chose retired General Nobuyuki Abe to inaugurate an independent foreign policy. The despatch characterizes Abe's ten-member inner cabinet as an uninspiring collection of bureaucrats and economic planners, with the notable exception of Navy Minister Zengo Yoshida and Konoe intimate Kakichi Kawarada.
subfiles.title: Tokyo Despatch No. 4126: 'Change in the Japanese Cabinet - The Resignation of Baron Hiranuma and the Appointment of General Abe as Prime Minister'

subfiles.about: Official instruction conveying Department commendation to Third Secretary Frank A. Schuler, Jr., for Tokyo Despatch No. 4126.
subfiles.from: George S. Messersmith (Assistant Secretary of State, Washington)
subfiles.summary: Messersmith instructs Grew to thank Schuler for drafting Despatch 4126, praising its thoughtful, clear, concise analysis of Japan's political change.
subfiles.title: Instruction No. 1820 to Tokyo Commending Despatch No. 4126
